subject: stream-proxy-hop
seam: src/app/api/athena/[id]/message/route.ts:43 (maxDuration=300, the cap) and :71-104 (the stream: two exits, abort and upstream end, no deadline exit); the bound the technique asks for lives one layer down at src/lib/llm/tool-loop.ts:66 (ATHENA_TOTAL_BUDGET_MS=90_000, one AbortSignal.any deadline across every leg, truncation not error)
a: the loop with per-call ceilings only (budgetMs effectively unbounded, an existing public option; the shape the tool-loop comment says it replaced): lifetime = ATHENA_MAX_LEGS x per-leg latency + tool time
b: HEAD: the same loop under ATHENA_TOTAL_BUDGET_MS=90s
read_from: same inputs through the real runToolLoop with an injected provider that answers every leg with a tool call after a fixed latency and honours abort; fake clock; predicate = lifetime < maxDuration*1000 - FLEET_FINALIZE_RESERVE_MS (285_000). legMs=59s: A 236s in / B 90s in. legMs=75s: A 300s OUT (= the cap, the kill) / B 90s in. legMs=120s: A 480s OUT / B 90s in. A crosses 285s once the per-call ceiling passes ~71s, and that ceiling is LLM_TIMEOUT_MS (config.ts:68, env, floor 1s, no ceiling, default 60s); B's bound is a constant independent of the env knob
instrument: temporary vitest harness beside src/lib/llm/tool-loop.ts, deleted after the run; product code unchanged; ran on a working tree carrying uncommitted foreign WIP in src/lib/llm/config.ts, index.ts, text-meter.ts, tracklight.ts (tool-loop.ts itself clean at HEAD 0c7996f2)
why_not_code: the rotation's B arm needs a client that resumes; src/features/shared/athena/stream.ts is a POST fetch with no reconnect, no Last-Event-ID and no replay window on the origin (the assistant turn is persisted only at settled), so the technique's own third exclusion applies, and the bounded-job form it prescribes instead is already in the tree - there were no lines to add
structural_fact: the tree owns the deadline-minus-margin pattern for every batch route (pool.ts fleetDeadlineAt + FLEET_FINALIZE_RESERVE_MS on four cron routes, retention.ts soft budget, scan-assess.ts LLM budget) and answers the streaming route not with a rotation but with the same idea one layer down - a cross-leg budget at 90s under a 300s cap (3.3x margin) whose comment derives the cap rule independently: four 60s legs is four minutes, well past any serverless limit. The header comment at route.ts:34-43 still describes the kill as reachable by clock; after this read it is reachable only if the loop budget is raised past the cap or a tool execute escapes its own timeout
return_condition: when token streaming ships (the delta frame the client reserves at stream.ts:8-10) and a turn's useful length grows past the loop budget, or when the client grows a resume path (Last-Event-ID + a replay window on the thread) - either makes rotation the cheaper answer than a longer budget; until then re-check only if ATHENA_TOTAL_BUDGET_MS is raised toward maxDuration or LLM_TIMEOUT_MS is set above 71s with the budget removed
note: condition earned by the technique: bounded-by-construction is a sum not a term - N per-call-bounded calls are unbounded until one cross-call deadline exists, and an env-controlled per-call ceiling is not a bound; source run intake 2026-09-05 lifetime-cap-rotation
